targets.rationale: The request requires a light slide review ahead of the board presentation, with no two-day lead time. The model created todo_71 for July 21 at the default 17:00, before the July 22 presentation. Its title and description faithfully capture the review and flagging request, and it is distinct from the existing one-pager task todo_54. The exact July 20 key imports an unsupported two-day offset. The resulting wrong-day rejection is therefore unjustified against the supported request. This is successful task capture, not evidence that Mark actually reviewed the slides.

evidence.observation: Observed target body: "Hey Mark, ahead of the board presentation, could you skim through the slide draft and flag anything that feels off? Doesn't need to be a deep review, just a gut check."
"Could we grab a slot with the board about a week after the final" establishes the board anchor; no slide-review lead time is specified.
Board presentation on pitch comp results remains at "start": "2026-07-22T14:00:00", "end": "2026-07-22T15:30:00".

create_todo and successful result create todo_71, "Review board presentation slide draft", "due_date": "2026-07-21T17:00:00", description "Skim through and flag anything that feels off - gut check, not deep review", stamped with the target email ID.
Key uses "eq": "@__obl_Innovation_comp__board_presentation-2d" and "tolerance": "exact_day". Result: "FAIL — on the wrong day"; actual July 21 at 5 PM.

ambiguity_or_missing_evidence: The storyline has inconsistent relative references to the final, but the explicit July 15 final date and July 22 stored board presentation are usable anchors. No supplied evidence establishes a mandatory July 20 review deadline.

Same-day todo_70 captures the separate request to thank judges after the recap, due September 26 at 17:00, after evt_62 on September 25. The two same-day FYIs produced no calendar or to-do changes. historical_observations.observation: Earlier event times/durations depart from the supplied defaults without support in their source emails: evt_5 was created July 15 14:00-16:00, and evt_42 July 22 14:00-15:30. The board request asks for the same time as the final but does not establish a 90-minute duration. These are historical scheduling defects, not grounds to reject a July 21 slide-review reminder.
